notes: Explore idea: Gaussian-process regression (Rasmussen & Williams 2006), the eleventh research-algorithms tool, taken from the research-tools candidate list. It has seven kernels, a constant or linear mean (vague prior, R&W 2.7), closed-form LOO, a projected L-BFGS optimiser with seeded restarts, a page with a Web Worker, a CLI and an agent call. Verification against scikit-learn 1.9.1 on NOAA Mauna Loa CO2 2010-2026 (201 months): LML, gradient, predictive mean and SD agree to ~1e-12 for all 7 kernels (tests use 1e-9). From scikit-learn's start and bounds, the fit reaches the same optimum in 5 kernels and a higher one in quasiperiodic (329.47 vs 328.62). For the periodic kernel it stops at the all-noise KKT corner (-285.21 vs scikit-learn's -58.37); that is documented and tested. Finding: a held-out 36-month forecast (fit 2010-01..2023-09) gave RMSE 2.47 ppm / 6% band coverage with a constant mean and 1.08 ppm / 42% with a linear mean, against 1.07 ppm for seasonal naive; leave-one-out coverage inside the data was 96%. The default is a linear mean. Browser smoke test (Playwright, 1280 and 390 px): example fit in about 18 s, no console errors, no horizontal scroll. Local checks: run_venture_tests.py gaussian-process-regression ok (23 s); check_post_links 0 broken; check_post_frontmatter ok; run_workflow_locally --for-changes: 10/12 workflows passed. sibling-links failed and was then fixed (siblings --check 0 orphans; siblings.test 20/20). pages.yml and portfolio-validate gave no verdict because a step was skipped locally (no built site, no base ref, no pytest), and portfolio-pages 'Test the site builder' ran out of the 300 s local budget. platform/pages node --test: 1,637/1,639 at first, then the launched.json fix took launched.test.mjs to 23/23.
